about: The structure of the breast as an anatomy and physiology textbook presents it: glandular lobes and lobules, lactiferous ducts, nipple and areola, fat, suspensory ligaments, pectoral fascia and lymphatic drainage towards the axilla. Both sides are drawn in one view, each lying on the pectoral fascia over the chest wall and following its curve. How far the breast projects is a drawing choice, not a measurement. Twelve lobes a side is a schematic count. Activity is a display index driven by the engine's oestradiol, progesterone, prolactin, oxytocin and pregnancy signals; it is not a measure of milk production, and lactation itself is not simulated.

GH14.label: Hall JE, Hall ME. Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th ed. Elsevier, 2021.

GRAYS42.label: Standring S (ed). Gray's Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice, 42nd ed. Elsevier, 2020.

parts.label: Glandular Lobes and Lobules
parts.summary: Milk-forming tissue arranged radially round the nipple
parts.function: The glandular tissue is arranged in lobes that radiate from the nipple, each made of many lobules whose small terminal units are the milk-forming alveoli. Oestrogen drives growth of the duct system and progesterone drives development of the lobules and alveoli, both rising through pregnancy. Prolactin then drives milk synthesis. The tissue brightens with these hormone signals.

drives.note: Oestrogen stimulates growth of the ductal system.
Progesterone stimulates lobule and alveolar development.
Prolactin stimulates milk synthesis by the alveolar cells.
The glandular tissue enlarges through pregnancy.

parts.label: Lactiferous Ducts
parts.summary: Ducts that converge on the nipple
parts.function: Each lobe drains by a lactiferous duct, and the ducts converge on the nipple, widening into a sinus just behind it before they open on its surface. Oxytocin makes the contractile cells round the alveoli squeeze milk into them (the let-down reflex). The ducts brighten with the oxytocin signal and a pale stream runs towards the nipple.

drives.note: Oxytocin contracts the myoepithelial cells that eject milk into the ducts.

parts.label: Nipple
parts.summary: Raised tip where the ducts open
parts.function: The nipple is the raised tip of the breast on which the lactiferous ducts open. It contains smooth muscle and is rich in sensory nerve endings, and stimulation of it is the trigger for oxytocin and prolactin release. It brightens with those signals.

drives.note: Nipple stimulation releases oxytocin from the pituitary.

parts.label: Areola
parts.function: The areola is the circle of pigmented skin round the nipple, containing small glands that lubricate it. It darkens during pregnancy. It brightens with the pregnancy signal.

parts.label: Adipose Tissue
parts.summary: Fat that fills the breast round the gland
parts.function: Fat fills the space between and around the glandular lobes and gives the breast most of its volume and shape. It is drawn as glass so the gland and ducts show through. Oestrogen promotes its deposition at puberty.

parts.label: Suspensory Ligaments
parts.summary: Fibrous bands from chest wall to skin
parts.function: Fibrous bands (Cooper's ligaments) run from the fascia on the chest wall to the skin, crossing the gland and fat. They support the breast without restricting it.

parts.label: Pectoral Fascia
parts.summary: Sheet over the chest muscle behind the breast
parts.function: The pectoral fascia is a sheet of connective tissue over the pectoralis major muscle. It lies behind the breast and is the surface to which the suspensory ligaments attach. It is drawn as glass because it only lines the back of the space.

parts.label: Lymphatic Vessels
parts.summary: Collecting vessels draining towards the axilla
parts.function: Lymph collects from the skin and the gland around the areola and drains outwards and upwards, mostly to the lymph nodes of the axilla. Lymph flow rises with muscular activity and with inflammation. A pale stream runs along them, faster when those signals rise.

drives.note: Inflammation increases fluid and lymph flow.

parts.label: Lymph Nodes towards the Axilla
parts.summary: Nodes at the upper outer edge of the breast
parts.function: Lymph passes through nodes on its way to the axilla, where they filter it and respond to what it carries. They are drawn at the upper outer edge of the breast, towards the armpit. They brighten with immune activation.

drives.note: Nodes respond to antigens carried in the lymph.

parts.label: Lactiferous Sinuses
parts.summary: The widened ends of the ducts just behind the nipple
parts.function: Each lactiferous duct widens into a sinus beneath the areola, where milk collects before it reaches the nipple. They are drawn as small swellings on the ducts.

drives.note: The let-down reflex moves milk towards the nipple.

parts.label: Areolar Glands (Montgomery)
parts.summary: The small glands in the areola that raise little bumps on the skin
parts.function: The areolar glands are large sebaceous glands in the areola. Their secretion lubricates the nipple and areola. They enlarge in pregnancy and are drawn as small bumps.

parts.label: Retromammary Space
parts.summary: The loose layer behind the breast, in front of the pectoral fascia
parts.function: The retromammary space is a layer of loose fatty tissue between the breast and the fascia over the muscle, which lets the breast move a little on the chest wall. It is drawn as a thin glass sheet.

parts.label: Axillary Tail
parts.summary: The extension of breast tissue towards the armpit
parts.function: The axillary tail (of Spence) is a tongue of glandular tissue that runs from the upper outer part of the breast towards the axilla, where the lymph nodes lie.

parts.label: Lobule
parts.summary: One small gland unit at the end of a lobe, with its own terminal duct
parts.function: A lobe ends in many lobules, each a cluster of tiny glands that make milk. One lobule is drawn here as a magnified glass sphere in each breast.

parts.label: Terminal Duct Lobular Unit
parts.summary: The small duct and the lobule of glands that it serves
parts.function: The terminal duct lobular unit is the working unit of the breast: the last small duct and the group of alveoli that open into it. It is drawn as a small branching duct. In the textbook the alveoli are part of the unit; they are listed beside it here to keep the list shallow.

parts.label: Alveoli
parts.summary: The tiny sacs of milk-secreting cells
parts.function: The alveoli are small sacs lined by secretory cells that make milk under the influence of prolactin. They are drawn as tiny beads at the ends of the branching duct.

parts.label: Myoepithelial Cells
parts.summary: The contractile cells that surround each alveolus
parts.function: The myoepithelial cells lie round each alveolus and the small ducts, and oxytocin makes them contract and squeeze milk out. They are drawn as a fine basket round each alveolus.
